Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt

Class Runtime

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt.Runtime
public final class Runtime extends Object
One Mandela engine: the pair a host actually holds, a VM and the StandardLibrary it asks questions of, wired to the host's console and capability set.

This is the class behind every other door into the language — the CLI, the REPL, the JSR-223 engine, an Espresso panel, a Web Browser page — and it exists so those doors stay three-line wrappers. A host configures a Runtime.Builder, then either run(String)s a program or call(java.lang.String, java.lang.Object...)s one named function after a setup script has defined it. Nothing here decides policy: Capabilities does that, and this class hands the same object to the machine and to the library so a refusal reads the same from both.

Why one engine is not one run

The global table is deliberately retained between calls, which is what makes a REPL session and an editor that re-runs a selection behave: let x = 1 at the top level compiles to a DEFINE_GLOBAL, so the binding outlives the body that made it. A run resets the machine's instruction budget and stack, not the names. A host that wants a clean slate builds a second engine — cheap, since the library tables are read-only after construction and may be shared through Runtime.Builder.library.

Modules

import runs a file in a child engine that starts with a copy of this engine's names and keeps whatever it binds. The child is a separate machine, so a module cannot write back into the importer's globals, cannot inherit a half-finished operand stack, and its budget is charged to the same Capabilities the importer was given. Cycles are refused rather than resolved by a half-built module map, because a language that answers undefined for a circular import turns a typo into a runtime bug.

    • evaluate

      public static Object evaluate(String source)
      A one-shot engine for a caller that has nothing to configure.

      The capabilities are Capabilities.console() — stdout and stderr and nothing else, never a file, a socket, a thread or the JVM. Use builder() the moment the run needs more than that.

      Parameters:
      source - the program
      Returns:
      the value of its last expression

    • run

      public Object run(CompiledFunction body)
      Runs a body this engine compiled earlier.

      Kept public because a host that compiles once and runs many times — a template, a per-keystroke check, a saved Espresso run configuration — should not have to re-parse the text on every pass. The names the body reads are resolved when it was compiled, so anything bound after that is invisible to it; compile last, run often.

      Parameters:
      body - the compiled program
      Returns:
      the value of its last expression

    • setOutput

      public void setOutput(Consumer<String> out, Consumer<String> err)
      Re-points the console after the engine was built.

      The builder sets the sinks once, which is right for a CLI; a JSR-223 engine and a browser page get a different writer per call, so they need to move the console without rebuilding the engine. Module children inherit the new sinks, which is what makes imported code print into the same panel as its importer.

      Parameters:
      out - where print and println go, or null for no console
      err - where eprintln and uncaught errors go, or null for none

    • check

      public List<Diagnostic> check(String source, String sourceName)
      Reports what is wrong with a program, without throwing.

      The editor calls this on every keystroke, so it is the one entry point that must never raise: a parse failure becomes a diagnostic, a compile failure becomes a diagnostic, and the caller gets the list either way.

      Parameters:
      source - the program text
      sourceName - the name to report under
      Returns:
      the findings, empty when the program is sound

    • bind

      public void bind(String name, Object value)
      Publishes one host value or function under a name.

      Call it before run for the best diagnostics: a name the compiler knows is a name it can type-check and an editor can complete.

      An ordinary Java value is widened the way HostValues does, so bind("limit", 10) means what it looks like and a Kotlin or Java lambda becomes a callable the script can call. A value with no Mandela form — a domain object — is refused here rather than surfacing three statements later as an arithmetic error about a Host.

      Parameters:
      name - the name a script will read
      value - the value, or anything with an obvious Mandela form
      Throws:
      MandelaError - when the value has no Mandela form

    • failureTrace

      public List<String> failureTrace()
      The frames a failure ran through on its way out of the last run.

      trace() answers the frames that are live now, which is nothing once the machine has unwound — so a host that reports a crash after catching it, the way the CLI does under --trace, has to ask for the snapshot the machine kept instead.

      Returns:
      the frames of the last uncaught failure, outermost first, or empty

    • knownGlobals

      public Set<String> knownGlobals()
      The names a program on this engine may read without declaring them: the library's globals, the host's bindings, and the use / import hooks.

      An editor builds its completion list and its "unknown name" squiggle from exactly this set, which is why it is public: an embedder that adds a host function should have its editor offer that function the moment the engine that will run it exists.

      Returns:
      a snapshot of the visible names, in no particular order

    • evalLine

      public Object evalLine(String line)
      Runs one REPL entry.

      Bindings survive because a top-level let compiles to DEFINE_GLOBAL; the instruction budget resets because each entry is its own run. The caller prints the value it returns, and prints nothing when the entry only declared something.

      Parameters:
      line - the entry, which may span several statements
      Returns:
      the value the entry produced, possibly null

    • evalEntry

      public Object evalEntry(String source, String name)
      Whether one REPL entry is worth echoing. A run that produced no value at all is silent, and a run that produced null prints null: the distinction is the difference between a declaration and an expression.
      Parameters:
      source - the entry
      name - the name to report under
      Returns:
      the value, or REPL_SILENT when nothing should be printed

    • loadModule

      public MandelaMap loadModule(Machine from, String path)
      Loads a Mandela file as a module and returns its exported names.

      The path is resolved through Capabilities.resolve(java.lang.String, java.lang.String), so a module can only be imported from inside the directory the host granted, and the FILE_READ grant is asserted first: a browser page that reaches import is told no before a single byte is read.

      Parameters:
      path - the literal path from the import statement
      Returns:
      a map of the names the module exported
